questions.knowledge_point: Solving for an Unknown Given Two Perpendicular Vectors
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $c⊥d$ ($c$ and $d$ are perpendicular) if and only if $c\cdot d=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d & ={c}_{x}\cdot {d}_{x}+{c}_{y}\cdot {d}_{y}+{c}_{z}\cdot {d}_{z} \\  & =k\cdot (-3)+2k\cdot 2+4\cdot 2 \\  & =-3k+4k+8 \\  & =k+8.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot d & =0 \\ k+8 & =0 \\ k & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for an Unknown Given Two Perpendicular Vectors
questions.problem: Let $p=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ n\end{aligned}]$ and $q=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}].$ Given that $p⊥q$, find the value of $n.$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $p⊥q$ ($p$ and $q$ are perpendicular) if and only if $p\cdot q=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y} \\  & =7\cdot 4+n\cdot (-4) \\  & =28-4n.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 28-4n & =0 \\ 28 & =4n \\ n & =7\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for an Unknown Given Two Perpendicular Vectors
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $a⊥b$ ($a$ and $b$ are perpendicular) if and only if $a\cdot b=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y} \\  & =2{x}^{2}\cdot 8+(-4)\cdot 4 \\  & =16{x}^{2}-16.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 16{x}^{2}-16 & =0 \\ 16{x}^{2} & =16 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the negative solution since we are told that $x>0.$ Therefore, $x=1.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for an Unknown Given Two Perpendicular Vectors
questions.problem: Let $g=[\begin{aligned}{r}^{2} \\ -1 \\ -6\end{aligned}]$ and $h=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ {r}^{2} \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Given that $g⊥h$ and $r<0$, find the value of $r.$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $g⊥h$ ($g$ and $h$ are perpendicular) if and only if $g\cdot h=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}g\cdot h & ={g}_{x}\cdot {h}_{x}+{g}_{y}\cdot {h}_{y}+{g}_{z}\cdot {h}_{z} \\  & ={r}^{2}\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot {r}^{2}+(-6)\cdot 2 \\  & =3{r}^{2}-{r}^{2}-12 \\  & =2{r}^{2}-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}g\cdot h & =0 \\ 2{r}^{2}-12 & =0 \\ 2{r}^{2} & =12 \\ {r}^{2} & =6 \\ r & =\pm \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the positive solution since we are told that $r<0.$ Therefore, $r=-\sqrt{6}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for an Unknown Given Two Perpendicular Vectors
questions.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ Given that $u⊥v$ and $a<0$, find the value of $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $u⊥v$ ($u$ and $v$ are perpendicular) if and only if $u\cdot v=0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{x}\cdot {v}_{x}+{u}_{y}\cdot {v}_{y}+{u}_{z}\cdot {v}_{z} \\  & =a\cdot a+2\cdot (-4)+4\cdot (-2) \\  & ={a}^{2}-16.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =0 \\ {a}^{2}-16 & =0 \\ {a}^{2} & =16 \\ a & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

We disregard the positive solution since we are told that $a<0.$ Therefore, $a=-4.$

canonical_examples.problem: Let $[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ t\end{aligned}]$. Given that $\mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b}$, find the value of $t$.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We know that $\mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b}$ ($\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are perpendicular) if and only if $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = 0.$

Computing the dot product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =4\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot 5+1\cdot t \\  & =-8-10+t \\  & =t-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ t-18 & =0 \\ t & =18\end{aligned}
$$
